Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
Which aspect of a planned economy might be viewed unfavourably by a consumer but favourably by a producer?

options.A: a bureaucratic system of decision-making
options.B: a long response time to changing economic events
options.C: an absence of incentives to work and to produce
options.D: an emphasis on the production of capital goods

questions.questionText: If the rate of inflation rises from 2% to 20%, which function of money is likely to be most affected?

options.A: medium of exchange
options.B: standard for deferred payment
options.C: store of value
options.D: unit of account

questions.questionText: Which statement would be classified by an economist as a positive statement?

options.A: Balancing the budget cannot be more important than reducing inflation.
options.B: Maintaining the real income of pensioners needs to be a priority.
options.C: The government should increase indirect taxation.
options.D: The government will not increase direct taxation.

questions.questionText: Which statement about price elasticity of supply is correct?

options.A: It cannot change in the short run.
options.B: It increases as the time period lengthens.
options.C: It is infinite in the momentary time period.
options.D: It is zero in the long run.

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of demand for a firm’s product is equal to one for all price changes. What would be the result of this?

options.A: A percentage increase in price will cause demand to fall by a larger percentage.
options.B: A percentage increase in price will cause demand to increase by the same percentage.
options.C: Quantity demanded will always be the same whatever the price.
options.D: The firm’s revenue will always be the same whatever the price.

questions.questionText: What leads to a downward shift of a normal supply curve?

options.A: a rise in the cost of transporting goods
options.B: a rise in the productivity of the labour force
options.C: a rise in the rate of sales tax on the good
options.D: a rise in the wage rate paid to workers

questions.questionText: A market is in equilibrium with 100 units of the product sold at a price of US$10 each. The price elasticity of supply for the product is +2.0 and the price elasticity of demand is –1.0. What will be the state of the market if a minimum price of US$11 is imposed?

options.A: an excess demand of 10 units
options.B: an excess demand of 30 units
options.C: an excess supply of 20 units
options.D: an excess supply of 30 units

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for meat in equilibrium at X. The cost of producing meat rises and there is a trend for consumers to change from meat to a vegan (non-animal) diet. What is the new market equilibrium? S S price 1

options.B: S C X A D D D D O quantity

questions.questionText: Goods X and Y are complements. What will be the effect on the equilibrium price and quantity of good X of an increase in the supply of good Y? equilibrium equilibrium price of X quantity of X

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: A private company achieves a producer surplus at the market equilibrium price. What might reduce the size of the private company’s producer surplus?

options.A: Private companies choose to prioritise profits over customer needs.
options.B: Private companies start to pay dividends out of profits.
options.C: The government fixes the price of electricity below the market price.
options.D: The private company supply curve becomes more elastic.

questions.questionText: How would an economist establish the market demand curve for a private good?

options.A: by adding consumer surplus to total expenditure
options.B: by combining individual demand curves horizontally
options.C: by combining the price elasticity of individual demands
options.D: by multiplying price by quantity demanded

questions.questionText: Knowledge of which combination of demand elasticities would be relevant to a firm trying to increase its revenue? price elasticity cross elasticity income elasticity of demand of demand of demand
What will definitely stop, following the nationalisation of an industry?

options.A: dividend payments to the industry’s shareholders
options.B: job losses among the industry’s workforce
options.C: price increases for the industry’s product
options.D: the closure of unprofitable factories in the industry

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect of the government introducing a subsidy on a product. S price 1 (US$) S D 0 100 120 quantity (million units) What are the effects of the subsidy on government spending and consumer spending? government spending consumer spending

options.A: increases by US$240 million decreases by US$40 million
options.B: increases by US$240 million decreases by US$200 million
options.C: increases by US$480 million decreases by US$40 million
options.D: increases by US$480 million decreases by US$200 million

questions.questionText: In the diagram, S and D are the initial supply and demand curves of a product.

The table shows sources of government revenue in a fiscal year for an economy. source of revenue $ billions sale of government assets 100 tax on self employed 1000 carbon tax on goods produced 100 corporate taxes 500 capital gains tax 100 goods and services tax 1000 air passenger tax 100 What is the total amount, in $ billions, of tax revenue raised by indirect taxes?
Education from 4 to 16 years of age in most developed economies is provided at zero price, financed from taxation. Why should the government do this?

options.A: In a free market, consumers have imperfect information so do not realise the full personal benefit of education.
options.B: In a free market, education is not considered to be a private good.
options.C: In a free market, consumers will be unwilling to pay for education.
options.D: In a free market, education is non-rival and non-excludable in consumption so zero output would be produced.

questions.questionText: What will cause a movement along an aggregate supply curve?

options.A: a rise in the demand for exports
options.B: a rise in the price of raw materials
options.C: a rise in the productivity of labour
options.D: a rise in the rate of sales tax

questions.questionText: A government devalues its fixed exchange rate. What is most likely to be its aim?

options.A: to improve the terms of trade
options.B: to increase the level of aggregate demand
options.C: to reduce a current account surplus
options.D: to reduce demand-pull inflation

questions.questionText: As part of its trade policy, a government subsidises the cost of machinery used to manufacture goods for export. How will this affect the balance of payments?

options.A: decrease the deficit on the capital account
options.B: decrease the deficit on the current account
options.C: increase the deficit on the capital account
options.D: increase the deficit on the current account

questions.questionText: What is correct about the causes of inflation?

options.A: Cost-push inflation can be caused by a rising exchange rate.
options.B: Cost-push inflation can be caused by lower indirect taxes.
options.C: Demand-pull inflation can be caused by a rising exchange rate.
options.D: Demand-pull inflation can be caused by lower direct taxes.

questions.questionText: The figures shown are from New Zealand’s balance of payments for 2017 according to data published by Stats NZ in September 2018. NZ$m capital account balance 1300 current account balance –7000 financial account balance 7600 goods balance –3000 services balance 5000 What was the value of the balancing item (net errors and omissions) in NZ$m?

Between 2011 and 2013, retailers reported that expenditure on domestically-produced and imported goods had reduced. This was because consumers did not take out loans as the economy was in a recession. What is the likely result of this?

options.A: a decline in the deficit in the trade account
options.B: a decline in the level of savings
options.C: a decline in the terms of trade
options.D: a decline in unemployment

questions.questionText: Increased international competition leads to a worsening in a country’s current account balance. In the absence of any offsetting factors, how is this likely to affect the exchange rate and domestic cost-push inflation? cost-push exchange rate inflation

options.A: appreciate decrease
options.B: appreciate increase
options.C: depreciate decrease
options.D: depreciate increase

questions.questionText: Why are higher interest rates together with increased taxation on expenditure likely to cause domestic deflation?

options.A: because the contractionary monetary policy will over-ride the expansionary fiscal policy
options.B: because the monetary and fiscal policies involved will reinforce each other
options.C: because the expansionary monetary policy will over-ride the contractionary fiscal policy
options.D: because the monetary and fiscal policies involved will cancel each other out

questions.questionText: Which policy aimed at correcting a balance of trade deficit is an expenditure-reducing policy?

options.A: depreciation of the currency
options.B: increased direct taxation
options.C: tax incentives for exporters
options.D: the imposition of protectionist tariffs

questions.questionText: Which policy will not cause a reduction in the rate of inflation?

options.A: increasing income tax
options.B: reducing government spending
options.C: reducing interest rates
